item.title: 'Economic D-Day'? The US has picked wrong script for sanctioning Iran
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
'Economic D-Day'? The US has picked wrong script for sanctioning Iran Comparing an illegal unilateral sanctions campaign with no basis in international law and no authorization from the UN Security Council to the allied landing in Normandy, one of the defining battles of the anti-fascist war, is an absurd analogy. Forcing a stalled military conflict into the arena of economic confrontation only underscores how few cards the US has left to play. On Monday local time, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced a new round of sanctions against Iran under a plan dubbed "operation economic outcast." What is particularly bizarre is the name he gave the campaign: "economic D-Day." Comparing an illegal unilateral sanctions campaign with no basis in international law and no authorization from the UN Security Council to the allied landing in Normandy, one of the defining battles of the anti-fascist war, is an absurd analogy. The substance of the campaign is to extend sanctions to the countries that do business with Iran, effectively seeking to "sever every economic lifeline" available to Tehran. International opinion generally sees this more as a US "remedial measure" after military means failed to deliver results. Bloomberg economics analysts described that it left "major questions outstanding." Forcing a stalled military conflict into the arena of economic confrontation only underscores how few cards the US has left to play. The US has steadily tightened sanctions on Iran since 1979, yet has never managed to force Tehran to submit. Now Washington is serving up the same old recipe with a familiar taste, merely under the new label of an "operation economic outcast" campaign. Although Iran's average daily oil exports have plunged from around 2 million barrels before the war to approximately 287,000 barrels in August, Tehran still holds the key strategic leverage of the Strait of Hormuz and has accumulated extensive experience in coping with sanctions for a long time. If nearly 50 years of sanctions failed to achieve the goal, can simply giving them a "D-Day" label finally make them work? Through secondary sanctions, the US is not merely deciding "who it will do business with," but attempting to dictate to other countries around the world "who they can do business with." In doing so, Washington is opening multiple fronts at once: waging an economic war against Iran while simultaneously fighting sanctions battles with China, India, Turkey and even its European allies. Bessent has even threatened that countries that fail to cooperate could be excluded from the dollar system. It is a blatant weaponization of the dollar, turning the global financial system into a tool of unilateral punishment. When one country can arbitrarily cut off another country's economic lifelines at will, the foundations of the international economic and trade system are undermined, ultimately eroding confidence in the dollar's global credibility. Economic sanctions often trigger unintended chain reactions. The international oil prices have risen by over 50 percent so far this year. Further tightening restrictions on Iran's oil exports would only push oil prices higher and intensify inflationary pressures, casting an even darker shadow over an already fragile global economic recovery. The Strait of Hormuz is one of the world's most important energy chokepoints, and any disruption there could trigger sharp volatility in global energy markets. When economic measures are used as instruments of war, the risks won't remain within the boundaries envisioned by the US. They will spread and spill over, ultimately leaving everyone to foot the bill. The most urgent task now is not to escalate confrontation, but to de-escalate the situation. Dialogue and negotiations are the only right path toward resolving the US-Iran War and the Iranian nuclear issue, and this is a broad consensus in the international community. Unilateral sanctions and threats of force will not help resolve the problem; instead, they will exacerbate tensions and narrow the space for diplomacy. The US should seriously reflect on the gains and losses of its policy toward Iran, rather than blindly pressing ahead down a path that has already been proven to be a dead end. The so-called "operation economic outcast" is itself a reflection of the predicament facing US policy. Even Washington may have little confidence in how effective the new sanctions will be. More importantly, today's world is no longer one in which a single country can unilaterally determine the fate of other countries. Global multipolarity is an irreversible historical trend, and countries making independent choices based on their own national interests is simply a basic fact of international relations. It should be noted that some US media outlets have deliberately sought to turn attention toward China, attempting to create a narrative that the success or failure of the campaign depends on whether China cooperates. The possibility that Washington could use the regional conflict to exert additional economic pressure on China warrants vigilance. China's cooperation with Iran has always been conducted within the framework of international law and should not be disrupted or undermined. China is not a party to US military actions against Iran or the Iranian nuclear issue, and should certainly not be held responsible for the failure of US policy. Some people in the US should focus on how to build "a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability," rather than constantly seeking to create turmoil in bilateral relations. In May this year, China's Ministry of Commerce, for the first time, issued a blocking ban under the rules on countering foreign states' unlawful extraterritorial jurisdiction measures, explicitly prohibiting any recognition, enforcement or compliance with US sanctions imposed on five Chinese companies on the grounds of their alleged involvement in Iranian petroleum transactions. China has a comprehensive range of legal and policy tools at its disposal and will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests. Any attempt to force China to submit through sanctions and pressure will not succeed. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China mulls road safety law revisions, law against cross-border corruption
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
China mulls road safety law revisions, law against cross-border corruption Zhao Leji, chairman of the National People's Congress (NPC) Standing Committee, presides over the first plenary meeting of the 24th session of the 14th NPC Standing Committee at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Aug. 25, 2026. (Xinhua/Pang Xinglei) BEIJING, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese lawmakers convened on Tuesday to review a raft of bills, including draft revisions to the Road Traffic Safety Law, a draft law on combating cross-border corruption and a draft healthcare security law. The bills were submitted for deliberation at the 24th session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress (NPC), the country's top legislature. Zhao Leji, chairman of the NPC Standing Committee, presided over the first plenary meeting of the session. In the meeting, lawmakers deliberated a draft healthcare security law. Submitted for a third reading, the draft includes provisions on long-term care insurance, aiming to further protect the rights and interests of insured people. A draft law on farmland protection and quality improvement was submitted for its third reading, adding provisions on talent cultivation and strengthening oversight of funds for high-standard farmland development. Lawmakers also reviewed a revised draft of the Agriculture Law, which improves support for agricultural and rural economic development, enhances protection for farmers' rights and interests, and strengthens rural development and governance. A draft revision to the National Defense Mobilization Law was submitted for its second reading. The revisions clarify the concept of national defense mobilization and rules on the collection, use and security management of relevant data. Lawmakers reviewed a draft amendment to the lawyers law that improves the provisions to boost foreign-related legal services. A revised draft of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, submitted for its second reading, refines rules on the bankruptcy of individual debtors bearing joint and several liability, improves the reorganization system, and adjusts the priority order for distributions from the bankruptcy estate. Also under review was a revised draft of the banking supervision and regulation law, which introduces classified and tiered supervision of banking institutions, improves the system for protecting banking consumers' rights and interests, and adds a separate chapter on risk resolution. Lawmakers also reviewed a revised draft of the Water Law. The second-reading draft strengthens provisions on the protection of water resources and water ecology, national water network development, and water conservation and recycling. Draft revisions to the Road Traffic Safety Law were submitted for review, seeking to improve the road traffic safety management system and strengthen the legal framework for maintaining traffic order. The draft includes a dedicated chapter on autonomous vehicles. A draft law on combating cross-border corruption was submitted for the first reading, aiming to prevent and punish transnational corruption, deepen international cooperation and safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests. Lawmakers also heard a series of reports, including a report on the implementation of the 2026 plan for national economic and social development, a report on budget execution, a report on government debt management in 2025, and a supervisory research report on government debt management in 2025. A report on improving the quality of cultural products and services and a report on efforts to consolidate and expand achievements in poverty alleviation and advance all-around rural revitalization were also on the agenda of the lawmakers. Lawmakers also deliberated an extradition treaty between China and Hungary, a deputy qualification report and personnel-related bills. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: China striving to ensure good start to 15th Five-Year Plan period: official
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
China striving to ensure good start to 15th Five-Year Plan period: official BEIJING, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- China is working to promote sustained economic development toward new and higher-quality growth with positive momentum, and striving to ensure a sound start to the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), said Wang Changlin, deputy head of the National Development and Reform Commission, on Tuesday. Entrusted by the State Council, Wang made the remarks when presenting a report on the implementation of the national economic and social development plan since the start of this year to the ongoing session of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the country's top legislature. Wang said China's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 4.7 percent year on year in the first half of 2026, with economic output increasing by 3.6 trillion yuan (530.57 billion U.S. dollars), marking the largest increase in five years for this period. Indicators including economic growth, employment, prices and foreign trade were in line with expectations, while consumption and residents' income maintained steady growth. China's economy has a stable foundation, many advantages, strong resilience and great potential. The underlying support conditions and the fundamental trend of long-term sound development remain unchanged, Wang noted. To do a good job in economic work in the second half of the year, Wang said China should adhere to the general principle of pursuing progress while ensuring stability, continue to deepen reform and opening up, and accelerate the transition from old growth drivers to new ones. China should effectively implement a more proactive fiscal policy and an appropriately accommodative monetary policy, make full use of existing policy measures, and introduce pragmatic and effective incremental policies in a timely manner, Wang added. Efforts should also be made to step up counter-cyclical adjustments, further expand domestic demand and optimize supply, and effectively safeguard and improve people's livelihoods, Wang said. item.title: China warns against unilateral sanctions after U.S. vows "economic asphyxiation" of Iran
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
China warns against unilateral sanctions after U.S. vows "economic asphyxiation" of Iran BEIJING, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- China has made clear on multiple occasions that it firmly opposes illegal unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and are not authorized by the UN Security Council, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said on Tuesday. Lin made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on media reports that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Monday laid out plans for the "economic asphyxiation" of Iran, expanding Washington's secondary sanctions threats and warning of dire consequences for countries that do not join the campaign. Economic warfare and maximum pressure do not help solve problems. Instead, they only escalate tensions and conflicts, create spillover risks, disrupt the global economic and financial order, and undermine the legitimate rights and interests of other countries, Lin said. The pressing priority now is to de-escalate the situation and return to the track of dialogue and negotiation as soon as possible, he added. China's cooperation with Iran is always conducted within the framework of international law and should not be disrupted or undermined, Lin said. China is closely following relevant developments and will take all necessary measures to resolutely safeguard its legitimate rights and interests, he noted. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Forest treasures become art in N China's Inner Mongolia
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
Forest treasures become art in N China's Inner Mongolia With her nose brushing against the dense pine needles, Fu Lihong seems to catch a glimpse of the vast pine forests before her. Each stroke in these artworks is not painted, but in fact created by carefully arranging pine needles, pine cones, and dried bark collected from the Greater Khingan Mountains, north China's Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. As a representative inheritor of the intangible cultural heritage of Mengxiaosong pine cone painting, Fu has a deep bond with the forest. Photo shows pine cone paintings created by Fu Lihong displayed at the forest culture art museum she founded. (People's Daily Online/Liu Yilin) Fu's father was a forestry worker. As a child, she often followed her father into the forest, where pine nuts were her favorite snack. Those childhood memories of running through the woods later became the inspiration for her creations. Since the 1950s, Arxan has carried out large-scale afforestation efforts. Fu's father was among those who planted trees at the time. By 1992, the preserved area of Arxan's artificial forests had reached 1 million mu (about 66,667 hectares). Materials used for making pine cone paintings are displayed at the art museum. (People's Daily Online/Liu Yilin) Trees planted by previous generations now provide shade for those who follow. What others see as withered branches and fallen leaves have become treasures in Fu's hands. Materials used for making pine cone paintings are displayed at the art museum. (People's Daily Online/Zhang Liyang) Over three years, Fu traveled through the forest across all four seasons, collecting large quantities of pine cones and leaves. After gathering nearly 1 million pine needles, she created a series of one-of-a-kind artworks. In 2021, Fu founded the Mengxiaosong Forest Culture Art Museum, the only museum in Inner Mongolia dedicated to pine tree culture. Photo shows pine cone creative cultural products displayed at the art museum. (People's Daily Online/Liu Yilin) The museum is more than just an exhibition space: Fu developed an art course which takes children into the forest to learn about plants in the Greater Khingan Mountains before returning to the museum to create their own pine cone paintings. In 2024, the course was recognized as an outstanding study-tour program in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. The museum has also created jobs for local residents. Fu hires forestry workers with spare time to collect pine cones and pine needles, which are then used in her creations. She is also training inheritors of the intangible cultural heritage craft, helping more people master the technique. An art course, developed by Fu Lihong, which takes children into the forest to learn about plants in the Greater Khingan Mountains, is an outstanding study tour program in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region. (People's Daily Online/Liu Yilin) Photo shows pine cone creative cultural products displayed at the art museum. (People's Daily Online/Liu Yilin) Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China reports steady consolidation of poverty alleviation gains
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
China reports steady consolidation of poverty alleviation gains A drone photo taken on May 15, 2026 shows a view of the tea gardens in Luxi Village of Jingde County, Xuancheng City, east China's Anhui Province. (Xinhua/Zhou Mu) BEIJING, Aug. 25 (Xinhua) -- China's poverty alleviation outcomes have been steadily consolidated and expanded, with rural per capita income showing a stable rise, a State Council report has revealed. The report on consolidating poverty alleviation achievements and advancing rural revitalization was submitted for deliberation at the ongoing session of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, the country's top legislature, which opened on Tuesday. According to the report, the per capita disposable income of rural residents in counties that have been removed from the poverty list rose from 12,588 yuan (about 1,855 U.S. dollars) in 2020 to 18,627 yuan in 2025, achieving average annual growth of 8.2 percent. It also noted marked improvements in rural infrastructure and public services, and a narrowing development gap compared with other regions. Industrial and employment assistance have been stepped up, and efforts have been made to stabilize jobs for those who have been lifted out of poverty. The number of such people with jobs has exceeded 32 million, the report said. The report also acknowledged persistent challenges, including long-term risks of relapse into poverty and weak development foundations in less-developed areas. Looking ahead, regular assistance will be integrated into the overall rural revitalization strategy, with people at risk of falling back into poverty and underdeveloped regions remaining as the primary targets of assistance. The approach will combine development-oriented support with a sound social security system to safeguard basic livelihoods, the report said. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: 2026 APEC SME ministerial meeting to focus on innovation, cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-25
2026 APEC SME ministerial meeting to focus on innovation, cooperation A themed installation is pictured at a business district in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Aug. 10, 2026. (Xinhua/Liang Xu) BEIJING, Aug. 24 (Xinhua) -- The 32nd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) Ministerial Meeting will be held on Sept. 4 in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT) said on Monday. The meeting, themed "innovation-driven development for win-win cooperation," will bring together SME officials from APEC economies, representatives of the APEC Secretariat, and other guests. The meeting will focus on technological innovation, digital empowerment and inclusive development, with a joint ministerial statement and other outcome documents expected, according to Liang Zhifeng, director of the SME bureau under the MIIT. As the host, China hopes that through in-depth exchanges, all economies will reach forward-looking and practical consensus, promote mutual learning of policies and the translation of outcomes, and jointly enhance the innovation capacity, digitalization level and sustainable development capabilities of SMEs in the Asia-Pacific region, said Vice Minister of Industry and Information Technology Ke Jixin. Wang Sheng, vice governor of Guangdong, said that all preparations for the meeting are essentially complete, and all APEC economies had confirmed their participation. More than 2,100 companies from home and abroad have registered for the accompanying exhibitions, with over 3,900 booths planned. China will host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in south China in November this year, which will mark the country's third hosting of the event following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. This year marks the APEC "China Year," with the theme of "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together." Approximately 300 APEC-related meetings and events will take place in multiple Chinese cities throughout the year. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
